summary: Leonard John Sedgwick (1883-1925) was an Indologist. He earned his B.A. studying at Pembroke College, University of Cambridge, from circa 1902 to 1905.

Leonard Swidler (1929-2026) worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at St. Norbert College, Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. ~1961), and Tübingen, he taught at Duquesne (1960-1966) and served as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966-2022).
Leonard Woolley (1880-1960) was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He was educated at St John's School, Leatherhead, and studied at New College from circa 1899 to 1903.
Leonard Zwilling (1948-2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1976.

Leonard van der Kuijp (b. 1952) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. and D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later serving at the University of Washington (~1987-1995) and Harvard University (1995).

Leonhard Masing (1845-1936) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer, Göttingen, and Leipzig under August Leskien (Ph.D. 1876). He later served at the University of Tartu as docent (1880-1910) and teacher (1918-1925).

Leonid Kulikov is a linguist and Indologist who earned his Candidate of Sciences from the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1989. He has held positions at Leiden, Ghent (assistant and guest professor 2011-2020), and KU Leuven (professeur, 2022).

Leonidas Clint (1812-1897) was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (M.A. ~1840). He served as Principal of La Martinière College (1845-1854) and Krishnagar Government College (until 1857).

Leopold Pospisil (1923-2021) studied at Charles University, Willamette, Oregon, and Yale (Ph.D. ~1956). He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and was curator of anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (~1956-1993).

Leopold von Ranke (1795-1886) was a historian who attended Schulpforta and studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig (1814-1818). He held a faculty post at the Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1871.

Leopold von Schroeder (1851-1920) was an Indologist who studied at Tartu, Tübingen, and Jena under scholars including Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu (1877-1894), Innsbruck (1894-1899), and Vienna (from 1899).

Leopoldo de Eguílaz y Yánguas (1829-1906) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned a doctorate in law at Complutense University of Madrid (~1858-1864) and was appointed Professor of General and Spanish Literature at the University of Granada in 1864.

Lepel Henry Griffin (1838-1908) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Windlesham House School and Harrow School (~1853-1856), and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1860 to 1889.

Leslie S. Kawamura (1935-2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. under Herbert V. Guenther at the University of Saskatchewan (~1971-1975) and served as a professor at the University of Calgary from circa 1976 until 2011.

Levi H. Elwell (1854-1916) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Amherst College (~1871-1875), studied at Yale University (1876-1877), and served as an Instructor in Latin at Amherst College (1877-1878).

Levi McLaughlin works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toronto, Tokyo under Susumu Shimazono, and Princeton (Ph.D. 2004-2009). He held fellowships at NUS and Iowa, becoming a professor at North Carolina State University in 2012.

Lewin Bentham Bowring (1824-1910) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College and Fort William College, served in the Bengal Civil Service (1843-1870), and was Chief Commissioner of Mysore (~1862-1870).

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA and PhD from SOAS. He held posts at Munich, NTNU (2018-2020), and Ruhr University Bochum, becoming Professor of Tibetology at the University of Bonn in 2021.

Lewis Hodous (1872-1949) was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies educated at Case Western Reserve, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served as head of Fukien Union Theological Seminary (1902-1917) and was a professor at Hartford Seminary (1917-1945).

Lewis Lancaster (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson at Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. 1968), served as professor at UC Berkeley from circa 1967, and was president at University of the West in 1992.
